newsitem.title: CHINA: SHENZHEN B INDEX LITTLE CHANGED AT NOON.
newsitem.headline: SHENZHEN B INDEX LITTLE CHANGED AT NOON.

text.p: Shenzhen's hard currency B share index inched up in quiet trade on Wednesday morning, with market attention focused on a flood of forthcoming interim results, brokers said.
The index gained 0.30 points or 0.22 percent to 133.54 on light turnover of HK$24 million.
The yuan-denominated A share index extended Tuesday's losses and fell 2.92 points or 0.77 percent to 377.49 on turnover of 1.4 billion yuan.
"The B share market is neither hot nor cold, and many investors are staying on the sidelines before the peak of the reporting season," an analyst at J&A Securities (HK) said.
Only eight out of the 49 Shenzhen B share listed companies have released their 1997 first half results despite the approach of the official August 30 deadline.
"Companies that make their results known early tend to be stronger, with the weaker ones usually reporting later," the J&A analyst said.
A strong performance by watchmaker Shenzhen Fiyta Holdings Ltd helped to lift the market mood, analysts said.
The issue ended the morning up 4.87 percent at HK$6.46, after peaking at HK$6.70 in mid-session, driven by an 85 percent surge in year-on-year interim net profits reported on Tuesday.
"A lack of buying interest in the market is restraining further advances by Fiyta," an analyst at China Southern Securities said.
In the B share market, Shenzhen Petrochemical (Holdings) Co Ltd was the strongest gainer and rose HK$0.15 or 6.52 percent to HK$2.45.
The A share market was depressed by recent releases of weak interim reports, athough the index was unlikely to fall much further after plunges in the last two days, analysts said.
Among A shares, automobile parts maker Zhuzhou Torch was the poorest performer, diving to its 10 percent limit-down level of 7.80 yuan.
